cases.title: memory-intent message retrieves the patient's provenance-labeled memory into context
cases.description: Phase 8 §22: a memory-intent message (deterministic trigger) with a server-resolved patient retrieves the PATIENT-domain memory. The block is bounded, provenance-labeled, and injected as a distinct section — never flattened into the structured record.

cases.title: AI_DERIVED conversation candidate is included only with an explicit UNVERIFIED label
cases.description: Phase 8 §17: conversation-scoped candidates (AI_DERIVED) are allowed when a conversation exists, but are ALWAYS rendered with the UNVERIFIED candidate label — never silently promoted to verified fact.

cases.title: no memory trigger → no memory retrieval (smallest-sufficient-context)
cases.description: Phase 8 §9: without a memory-intent signal or a case-level profile, the loop never queries memory — no retrieval, no block in context.

cases.title: explicit patient preference statement → deterministic USER_PROVIDED write (scope = own patient)
cases.description: Phase 8 §20: an explicit preference statement from a PATIENT actor writes ONE deterministic pref.* memory (USER_PROVIDED, patient scope = the session-resolved patient, retention applied). The LLM never chooses trust/class/scope.

cases.title: memory disabled (service absent) → run completes without any memory stage
cases.description: Phase 8 §9/§25: memory is an optional enhancement. Without a memory service the loop runs exactly as before (no retrieval, no update, no error).

cases.title: injection embedded in a stored memory value stays inert labeled data
cases.description: Phase 8 §21: untrusted/poisoned text stored in memory is rendered ONLY as a provenance-labeled data line. The deterministic agent does not follow instructions embedded in memory content (no cross-patient tools, no other patient's data in the answer).

cases.title: cross-tenant memory rows are never retrieved (tenant is part of every query)
cases.description: Phase 8 §15: memory queries are ALWAYS tenant-pinned. A tenant-B patient memory must never appear for a tenant-A actor, even when the message has a memory trigger.

cases.title: implicit preference (no explicit statement) → NO memory write (deterministic gate)
cases.description: Phase 8 §20: only EXPLICIT preference statements write memory. Implicit/vague phrasing produces no write — the agent must not guess durable facts.
